raw_response:
I will still do it much like last year: I will not gamble on some big change at my age. Five mu is not big, and with only two people at home, I have to keep the work steady and the spending tight. I will split the land between spring maize and cotton so I do not put everything on one crop. For seed, I will buy the kind people around me plant when I see it comes up even and gives a full ear or good bolls. For fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than watch the field turn yellow and lose harvest. I have well water, so I will use it when the crop is at the stage that matters, not wait for the sky. Maize I will keep simpler because it is quicker and easier to manage. Cotton needs more watching, more spraying, and more topdressing, but if I manage it cleanly it can still bring money. I will plough before planting, put most of the phosphate and potash in first, then add nitrogen in splits. I will do what I have seen work on nearby fields: maize gets fewer waterings and fewer sprays, cotton gets more careful management.
